body.p: The AI Positron add-on installed in can act as a local MCP (Model Context Protocol) HTTP server, allowing third-party AI assistants such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Open Code or Cursor to connect and use all tools defined and contributed by AI Positron, including tools to validate XML, refactor, run XPath, find in files, read and edit content, including access to the current editor context (opened project, files, current edited files, current selection).

Configure and start the server in the
Preferences Plugins / Oxygen AI Positron / Oxygen MCP Server page.

dd.p: The port number on which the local MCP HTTP server listens for incoming connections. Change this value if the default port is already in use by another application.

A button that starts or stops the local MCP HTTP server. The first time you click Start, you must accept a End User License Agreement (EULA) before the server can run. After the initial acceptance, subsequent starts and stops do not display the EULA again.

When the server is running, third-party AI assistants can discover and call the tools provided by AI Positron.The server must be started manually each time you re-start the application.The MCP HTTP server can only be started if you are using Enterprise version or the AI Positron Enterprise license.

Copies the MCP configuration JSON to the clipboard. Paste this configuration into your AI assistant's MCP settings to establish the connection. The copied configuration includes the port and an unique authentication token. Once added, the AI assistant will be able to discover and call the XML tools available in AI Positron add-on.

section.title: Preview File Changes
section.p: To have display a preview dialog whenever MCP tools modify or save content, add the following HTTP header to the MCP server configuration in your AI assistant:
When this header is present, each edit or save operation performed through MCP tools triggers a visual preview dialog in , allowing you to review the changes before they are applied.
